title: Simulation & Training
subtitle: Practice with lifelike make-believe APRS traffic that fills your map and station list but never touches the air.
in_this_chapter: What Simulation Mode makes and where it shows up
The Start / Pause / Resume / Stop / Step / Reset controls
The default mix of stations, objects, weather, and messages
Training Mode: guided scenarios with task checklists
Why nothing here can ever transmit
Troubleshooting when you don't see the fake traffic

blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: **Simulation Mode** and **Training Mode** let you learn APRS Command with the whole app doing something. Instead of staring at an empty map waiting for a real station to come by, you turn on Simulation and the map fills with made-up stations moving around, a weather station reporting, an object or two, and some message and bulletin traffic. Everything lands on the __map page__, the station list, and the packet monitor exactly like real received traffic, so you can practice finding stations, opening their details, and reading packets.

**Training Mode** goes one step further: it wraps that fake traffic in a guided __scenario__ with a short checklist of practice tasks ("Locate SIM001 on the map", "Open station details"), so a newcomer has something concrete to do and a way to track progress.

callout.label: Nothing here goes on the air
callout.text: Both modes are transmit-safe by design. The title bar keeps showing the **TX Disabled** badge, and each panel shows **Simulation transmit disabled** / **Training transmit disabled** in teal. The simulated packets are generated inside the app and fed into your display only — they are never keyed up on the radio or sent to APRS-IS. This is a fixed, built-in safety property, not a setting you can flip off by accident.

blocks.p: Simulation and Training each have their own panel in the feature tab area at the lower-right of the __map page__ — the same place **Replay** lives. Click the **Simulation** tab or the **Training** tab to bring up its controls. The map, station list, packet monitor, event logs, alerts, and weather panels all keep running while a session plays, so you can watch the fake traffic flow into every part of the app.

callout.label: Source-tagged
callout.text: Every simulated packet is tagged with the source `Simulation` so it stays clearly separated from live APRS-IS or RF data in the logs and packet monitor. Training scenarios that use simulated data are tagged the same way.

blocks.p: The **Simulation Mode** panel has a row of buttons across the top and a running list of the most recent generated packets at the bottom. The state (Stopped, Starting, Running, Paused, or Faulted) shows on the right of the title.

steps: Open the **Simulation** tab in the lower-right feature area.
Click **Start**. The state changes to `Running` and the first batch of simulated stations, objects, weather, messages, and bulletins is generated and pushed to the map and station list.
Watch the map fill in. Use **Pause** to freeze generation and **Resume** to continue where you left off.
Click **Step** to generate exactly one more batch by hand — handy when you want to advance slowly and study each update.
Click **Stop** when you're done. To wipe the generated packets and start clean (including re-homing the moving stations), click **Reset**.

blocks.p: Below the buttons the panel spells out what the run contains: the source name (**APRS Simulation**), the station count (for example `3 fixed / 2 mobile / 1 weather`), the update interval (`30 sec` by default), and the coverage area as a center latitude/longitude with a radius in meters. If anything goes wrong, an error line appears in red.

With the built-in defaults, each generated batch includes a handful of fixed stations with status text, moving mobile stations, a weather station, an object, and some message and bulletin traffic. The made-up callsigns are deliberately obvious so you never confuse them with real stations:

rows: A stationary simulated station with a position beacon
A status text packet for that station
A station that moves between batches (up to 45 knots by default)
A simulated weather report (wind, gusts, and so on)

blocks.p: The bottom of the panel shows **Recent simulated packets** with a scrolling list — each row gives the local time, the kind, the entity name, the source, and the raw packet text — so you can see exactly what was generated.

callout.label: Defaults are a starting point
callout.text: Out of the box a run covers roughly 3 fixed, 2 mobile, and 1 weather station plus 1 object, updating every 30 seconds, centered on the built-in area with a 10 km (10000 meter) radius and moving stations enabled. That mix is chosen to exercise most of the app at once.

blocks.p: **Training Mode** turns the fake traffic into guided practice. The left side lists the built-in __scenarios__ (each with a name, difficulty, and type); the right side shows the selected scenario's description, a progress readout, its task checklist, and a running event log.

steps: Open the **Training** tab. If the state reads `Disabled`, click **Enable** first — the state moves to `Ready`.
Pick a scenario from the list on the left. Its description and tasks appear on the right.
Click **Start**. The scenario begins and, where it uses simulated or replayed data, that data source starts automatically. The state shows `Running`.
Work the checklist under **Scenario Tasks**. Select a task and click **Complete** when you've done it, or **Skip** to pass. Progress updates as `X / Y tasks (Z%)`.
Use **Pause** / **Resume** to hold and continue, **Stop** to end the run, and **Reset** to set every task back to not-started and re-home the data.
Click **Disable** when you're finished to turn Training Mode off entirely.

blocks.p: The built-in scenarios range from **Beginner** (map familiarization, tracking mobile stations, watching a simulated weather station) through **Intermediate** (messaging practice, object placement, geofence entry/exit, replay review) to **Advanced** (alert-response practice). Each carries a short task list so a new operator always knows the next thing to try. Completing or skipping every task marks the scenario `Completed`.

callout.label: Training rides on Simulation and Replay
callout.text: A scenario feeds itself using the same transmit-safe simulation engine and, for the replay-review scenario, the Replay engine. Because both underlying sources are transmit-disabled, Training Mode is transmit-safe too.

blocks.p: Both are transmit-safe ways to see traffic without a live radio, but they are not the same tool. Use this to pick the right one:

rows: Freshly invented by the app as it runs
A previously recorded log of real packets
The exact same packets every time
Filling an empty map to learn the interface

blocks.p: In short: reach for **Simulation** when you just want lifelike activity to practice against, and **Replay** when you want to step back through a real recording. **Training** can use either one behind a guided checklist.

blocks.h1: Practice vs. a Real On-Air Exercise

blocks.p: It is natural to assume **Exercise Mode** (on the **Tools** menu) is what you switch on to run a drill with other operators. It is actually the opposite, and the difference is worth understanding.

**Exercise Mode means nothing transmits.** It is a safety lock for *rehearsing*: you can watch stations, send a message, place an object, and run a whole net, and none of it reaches the air. Everything you "send" appears in your own Raw Packet Monitor marked **Blocked**, so you can confirm you did it correctly — but no other station receives it. The lifelike traffic you practice against comes from **Simulation**, **Replay**, or **Training**; the app is generating those stations for you, not hearing them from other operators.

**To actually communicate with other stations in a drill, leave Exercise Mode off and enable transmit.** Talking to another station means putting a signal out, by definition. To keep your practice traffic from cluttering the live nationwide network or being mistaken for a real emergency, run the drill on a dedicated exercise or simplex frequency, or point everyone's APRS-IS connection at a private server, and note "drill" or "exercise" in your beacon comment.

callout.label: The name is the trap
callout.text: "Exercise Mode" guarantees you will NOT transmit — it is for safe practice, not for a drill where people talk to each other. For a real communicating exercise, turn Exercise Mode off, enable transmit, and use an exercise frequency or a private APRS-IS server.

bullets: **Started Simulation but the map is empty.** Confirm the state reads `Running` (not `Stopped` or `Paused`), then check your map filters and the station list — the simulated stations use obvious names like `SIM001` and `TESTWX1`. Zoom out or center the map on the simulation area if the stations are off-screen.
**The simulated stations aren't moving.** Movement advances one batch at a time. Wait for the update interval (30 seconds by default), or click **Step** to force the next batch immediately.
**A red error line appeared and the state says `Faulted`.** Click **Stop**, then **Reset**, and **Start** again to begin a clean run.
**Training buttons seem to do nothing.** Training must be enabled and a scenario selected first. Click **Enable** (state should read `Ready`), pick a scenario on the left, then click **Start**.
**Training progress or tasks look stale.** Click **Reset** to set every task back to not-started and reset the scenario's data, then start it again.

**Worried something might transmit.** It can't. The **TX Disabled** badge stays in the title bar and each panel shows its transmit-disabled line the entire time — Simulation and Training never key the radio or reach APRS-IS.
